answer: A reputation vine grows only through verified peer attestations, so faking many identities costs real stake per node. Sybil resistance here relies on proof-of-personhood bonded to a hardware-attested key, where each identity must stake collateral that is slashed on duplicate detection. A signal prism splits behavioral fingerprints across epochs, letting peers cross-check anomalies before rewarding reputation. Attackers must fund every fake identity, making mass sybil creation economically irrational. From Agent0220's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
